reason: TypeScript defect, reported 2026-11-12, fix pending on main. parsePlaceholderMap reads ANCHOR_MAP[bodyPr anchor] on a plain object (placeholder.ts:233), so anchor="constructor", "toString", "hasOwnProperty", "valueOf" give a function and "__proto__" gives Object.prototype as the anchor; the entry then exists where it should not, and resolvePlaceholderAnchor and the fill and preset-geometry matching follow it. Rust answers for the map's own anchors only.

reason: TypeScript defect, reported 2026-11-12, fix pending on main. chart.ts reads every CT_Boolean element (c:delete, c:showVal, c:smooth, c:rAngAx, c:overlay, ...) as val === '1' or val !== '0', so val="true" reads false at the first kind, val="false" reads true at the second, and an element without val (true by ECMA-376) reads false at the first kind. Rust reads those three forms by the schema through one helper, xsd_bool, and keeps the TypeScript reading for an absent element and any other val. The class is named by a test in calls-chart.ts (listed); these are its built inputs.

reason: TypeScript defect, found 2026-11-12 by the C1 comparison, to report to main. insert.ts reads IMAGE_MIME[ext] on a plain object, so an extension `constructor` (or another inherited name) is taken for an image type: addImageMediaAndRel writes ppt/media/imageN.constructor with a Default content type holding a function's source text and a relationship, and addPicture adds a picture element. Rust accepts only the own image extensions: no part, no relationship, no element (null).

reason: TypeScript defect, found 2026-11-12 by the C1 comparison, to report to main. layout.ts reads PH_HINT_MAP[type] on a plain object, so `<p:ph type="constructor"/>` (or toString, hasOwnProperty, valueOf) gives a function as the placeholder hint. Rust answers no hint for a type the map does not own.

cases.text: <p:sp><p:nvPr><p:ph type="constructor"/></p:nvPr><a:xfrm><a:off x="1" y="2"/><a:ext cx="3" cy="4"/></a:xfrm></p:sp><p:sp><p:nvPr><p:ph type="toString"/></p:nvPr><a:xfrm><a:off x="1" y="2"/><a:ext cx="3" cy="4"/></a:xfrm></p:sp><p:sp><p:nvPr><p:ph type="hasOwnProperty"/></p:nvPr><a:xfrm><a:off x="1" y="2"/><a:ext cx="3" cy="4"/></a:xfrm></p:sp><p:sp><p:nvPr><p:ph type="valueOf"/></p:nvPr><a:xfrm><a:off x="1" y="2"/><a:ext cx="3" cy="4"/></a:xfrm></p:sp>

reason: TypeScript defect, found 2026-11-12 by the C1 comparison, to report to main. notes.ts unescapeXml decodes the numeric character references first and the named entities after them, so the text `&lt;` (which is `<` as text) becomes `<`, and `&amp;` becomes `&`: a note or comment that contains an entity name as text loses it. Rust reads the text once, left to right.
